page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by ARMv9 architecture AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors. The system delivers 192 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 100 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this platform.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across highly parallelized workloads. The multi-core stress-ng metric reaches 380,524.27, placing it in the top tier alongside a PassMark CPU score of 107,915.98. The server exhibits high memory performance, delivering 725.79 GB/sec read throughput and 330.7 GB/sec write throughput on large uncached memory blocks. Application-level tests reflect these throughput strengths, achieving 520.51 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 355.34 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and top-tier metrics for PassMark database operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

While parallel compute and memory bandwidth are pronounced, single-core execution reflects mid-range positioning, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 2,013.79. In AI inference evaluations without hardware acceleration, prompt processing achieves top-tier throughput for small and medium models (3,957.91 and 381.5 tokens/sec, respectively), but generative token production lags, falling to 27.04 tokens/sec on smaller models.

This server type offers dense resource consolidation by combining 192 dedicated ARM cores, extensive DDR5 bandwidth, 100 Gbps networking, and 11.4 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage. It is targeted at scale-out in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data-intensive microservices, high-traffic web serving tiers, and batch compression or decompression pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server featuring 192 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 100 Gbps baseline networking. Without hardware GPUs, the platform relies on pure CPU throughput and high-bandwidth memory, recording top-tier results in multi-core stress testing (380,524.27), PassMark database operations (62,496.61), and Redis SET transactions (520.51 million ops/sec). The system features balanced 4.0 GB per-core memory capacity alongside high sustained memory bandwidth, though single-core performance and generative text generation remain moderate. Given its large local storage footprint and extensive core density, the server is well-matched for distributed in-memory databases, caching infrastructure, high-throughput static web serving, and heavy parallel data processing.
